## 1.outline
north korea**This is the highest level title and decoration, and** its official name **is ‘Hero of the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea.’** It is easy to see that it is an imitation of the Hero of the Soviet Union , and was enacted on June 30, 1950, during the Korean War . At the time of enactment, he was considered a ‘Hero of the People’s Republic of Korea’.[[3]](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EA%B3%B5%ED%99%94%EA%B5%AD%EC%98%81%EC%9B%85#fn-3) The name was used. The first date the Hero of the Republic Medal was awarded was July 15, 1950, 15 days after it was established, and 12 people received it simultaneously.
The Hero of the Republic Medal has a star surrounded by a circle inside a gold five-pointed star similar to the Order of Kim Il Sung or Order of Kim Jong Il , and the star shape is the same as that of the Hero of the Soviet Union. When attaching it to clothes, connect metal pins with white lines on the left and right edges on a red background and attach it to the right side of the top (left side of the wearer).

## 2.Detail
> Article 1. The title of Hero of the People's Republic of Korea is the highest honor in the Democratic People's Republic of Korea and is awarded to those who have individually or collectively performed heroic feats in front of the state.  
>   
> Article 2. The title of Hero of the North Korean People's Republic is awarded by the Presidium of the Supreme People's Assembly of North Korea .  
>   
> Article 3. In addition to this title, the Hero of the People's Republic of Korea is awarded the First Class Gold Star Medal of the Order of the National Flag and a commendation from the Presidium of the Supreme People's Assembly of Korea.  
>   
> Article 4. If a person who has been awarded the title of Hero of the People's Republic of Korea has repeatedly performed heroic feats worthy of being titled a Hero of the People's Republic of Korea, a second gold star medal is awarded, and in addition, a meritorious service is awarded to the hero's hometown to praise and commemorate his heroic feat. erect a statue of In this case, a commendation from the Presidium of the Supreme People's Assembly of Korea is also awarded.  
>   
> Article 5. The annual pension for the First Class Order of the National Flag received simultaneously with the conferment of the title of Hero of the People's Republic of Korea shall be double the stipulated amount.  
>   
> Article 6. The title of Hero of the People's Republic of Korea is awarded even in the case of the death of a person who has performed heroic exploits .  
>   
> Article VII. A person who has been awarded the title of Hero of the People's Republic of Korea enjoys all privileges and rights according to the provisions of the Order of the National Flag of the 1st, 2nd and 3rd classes.  
>   
> Article 8. The title of Hero of the People's Republic of Korea can only be revoked by the Standing Committee of the Supreme People's Assembly of Korea.  
>   
> Article 9. The gold star medal is worn on the upper left chest.  
>   
>   
>   
> * * *  
>   
>   
> **Provisions for the title of Hero of the People's Republic of Korea**

## 2.Detail
The title of Hero of the Republic is mainly awarded to soldiers with special expertise. In addition to soldiers, it is also awarded to high-ranking politicians, railroad workers, security guards (police officers), etc., and very occasionally it is awarded to organizations, institutions, buildings, or objects other than people. . In addition, perhaps because it has the same characteristics as South Korea's Grand Order of Rose of Sharon, it was also awarded to leaders of North Korea's allies, such as Fidel Castro , Hosni Mubarak **,****Pol Pot** , **and Mengistu Haile Mariam** , but Putin, who visited North Korea in 2024, was awarded the Kim Il-sung Medal rather than the Hero of the Republic. It appears that the policy has changed.
According to North Korea, a total of 627 soldiers of the Korean People's Army were awarded the title of Hero of the Republic for their meritorious service during the Korean War.[[4]](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EA%B3%B5%ED%99%94%EA%B5%AD%EC%98%81%EC%9B%85#fn-4)[[5]](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EA%B3%B5%ED%99%94%EA%B5%AD%EC%98%81%EC%9B%85#fn-5) , generally, kill 50 or more enemies or[[6]](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EA%B3%B5%ED%99%94%EA%B5%AD%EC%98%81%EC%9B%85#fn-6) It is said that one could receive it by accumulating special merits that could be used as propaganda material . As it was a difficult title to obtain, while some soldiers received it while alive, there were also many cases where it was awarded posthumously after death.
And at the time of the Korean War, there were soldiers who were awarded the title even though they were not in the North Korean army, and there were soldiers who were awarded the title among the Chinese troops who supported North Korea . According to the Chinese side, during the Korean War, a total of 12 Chinese soldiers were awarded the title of Heroes of the Republic.

## 2.Detail
In addition, when there is a national congratulation for a kind of 'enhancement of national prestige', the number of recipients other than soldiers increases rapidly. In December 2012, satellite A typical example is when as many as 201 scientists and those involved in satellite development/launch were simultaneously awarded after the successful launch of Kwangmyongsong-3 . After conducting the fourth underground nuclear test in January 2014, the same title was awarded to 200 officials.

## 2.Detail
Apart from such cases, it is very rare for this title to be conferred. In the case of female marathon runner Jung Sung -ok , who won the World Championships, she was originally scheduled to be awarded the title of Hero of Labor rather than Hero of the Republic . However, she received this title after enthusiastically praising Kim Il-sung and Kim Jong-il in an interview with foreign media after the competition, stating, "My victory is entirely thanks to our Great Leader and General." It is not as if she received the title of Hero merely for words like that.[[7]](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EA%B3%B5%ED%99%94%EA%B5%AD%EC%98%81%EC%9B%85#fn-7) To explain the full version, Kim Jong-il was moved by the fact that when asked about his feelings on winning, he said, “I recalled the image of the Great Leader calling out to me at the finish line, so I gave it my all until the end.” In addition to the title of Hero of the Republic, he was also awarded a Mercedes-Benz 400 and a luxury house in Pyongyang, and reportedly took home the entire $50,000 prize money.[[8]](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EA%B3%B5%ED%99%94%EA%B5%AD%EC%98%81%EC%9B%85#fn-8) Female judoka Kye Sun-hui, who won six gold medals in international competitions, is also a Labor Hero. Given that North Korea is obsessed with earning foreign currency prize money, it is highly unlikely that they would normally give the money to the athlete as is rather than confiscate it; thus, they gave her top-tier treatment with just a single word. However, a few years later, she reportedly confessed to the Chosun Sinbo , "I gained strength and won while looking at the wristwatch my lover personally put on my wristwatch," and it seems the Great Chairman of the National Defense Commission was completely fooled by words that were nothing more than lip service.

## 2.Detail
Recipients are supposed to receive the First Class Order of the National Flag at the same time, and like the Order of the Hero of the Soviet Union, it can be awarded to foreigners as well. At the same time, half-length statues are basically erected in the hometown or graveyard of the recipient, and it is not uncommon for there to be a school or factory named after the recipient . In the case of a military award, the name of the recipient and the hero title are added to the name of the unit to which the recipient belongs.[[9]](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EA%B3%B5%ED%99%94%EA%B5%AD%EC%98%81%EC%9B%85#fn-9)
It is the same with other North Korean medals, but negative perception continues to spread as the number of poor stars and other high-ranking people who receive awards for political considerations without much major is increasing . Maybe that's why, among the families of the Republic Hero + Honorary Soldier combo, there are cases where you have to resell 'beer tickets' to make a living...
It was once listed on eBay for $ 2,500 .

north korea**This is the highest level title and decoration, and** its official name **is ‘Hero of the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea.’** It is easy to see that it is an imitation of the Hero of the Soviet Union , and was enacted on June 30, 1950, during the Korean War . At the time of enactment, he was considered a ‘Hero of the People’s Republic of Korea’.[[3]](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EA%B3%B5%ED%99%94%EA%B5%AD%EC%98%81%EC%9B%85#fn-3) The name was used. The first date the Hero of the Republic Medal was awarded was July 15, 1950, 15 days after it was established, and 12 people received it simultaneously.
The Hero of the Republic Medal has a star surrounded by a circle inside a gold five-pointed star similar to the Order of Kim Il Sung or Order of Kim Jong Il , and the star shape is the same as that of the Hero of the Soviet Union. When attaching it to clothes, connect metal pins with white lines on the left and right edges on a red background and attach it to the right side of the top (left side of the wearer).

## 2.Detail
> Article 1. The title of Hero of the People's Republic of Korea is the highest honor in the Democratic People's Republic of Korea and is awarded to those who have individually or collectively performed heroic feats in front of the state.  
>   
> Article 2. The title of Hero of the North Korean People's Republic is awarded by the Presidium of the Supreme People's Assembly of North Korea .  
>   
> Article 3. In addition to this title, the Hero of the People's Republic of Korea is awarded the First Class Gold Star Medal of the Order of the National Flag and a commendation from the Presidium of the Supreme People's Assembly of Korea.  
>   
> Article 4. If a person who has been awarded the title of Hero of the People's Republic of Korea has repeatedly performed heroic feats worthy of being titled a Hero of the People's Republic of Korea, a second gold star medal is awarded, and in addition, a meritorious service is awarded to the hero's hometown to praise and commemorate his heroic feat. erect a statue of In this case, a commendation from the Presidium of the Supreme People's Assembly of Korea is also awarded.  
>   
> Article 5. The annual pension for the First Class Order of the National Flag received simultaneously with the conferment of the title of Hero of the People's Republic of Korea shall be double the stipulated amount.  
>   
> Article 6. The title of Hero of the People's Republic of Korea is awarded even in the case of the death of a person who has performed heroic exploits .  
>   
> Article VII. A person who has been awarded the title of Hero of the People's Republic of Korea enjoys all privileges and rights according to the provisions of the Order of the National Flag of the 1st, 2nd and 3rd classes.  
>   
> Article 8. The title of Hero of the People's Republic of Korea can only be revoked by the Standing Committee of the Supreme People's Assembly of Korea.  
>   
> Article 9. The gold star medal is worn on the upper left chest.  
>   
>   
>   
> * * *  
>   
>   
> **Provisions for the title of Hero of the People's Republic of Korea**

## 2.Detail
The title of Hero of the Republic is mainly awarded to soldiers with special expertise. In addition to soldiers, it is also awarded to high-ranking politicians, railroad workers, security guards (police officers), etc., and very occasionally it is awarded to organizations, institutions, buildings, or objects other than people. . In addition, perhaps because it has the same characteristics as South Korea's Grand Order of Rose of Sharon, it was also awarded to leaders of North Korea's allies, such as Fidel Castro , Hosni Mubarak **,****Pol Pot** , **and Mengistu Haile Mariam** , but Putin, who visited North Korea in 2024, was awarded the Kim Il-sung Medal rather than the Hero of the Republic. It appears that the policy has changed.
According to North Korea, a total of 627 soldiers of the Korean People's Army were awarded the title of Hero of the Republic for their meritorious service during the Korean War.[[4]](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EA%B3%B5%ED%99%94%EA%B5%AD%EC%98%81%EC%9B%85#fn-4)[[5]](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EA%B3%B5%ED%99%94%EA%B5%AD%EC%98%81%EC%9B%85#fn-5) , generally, kill 50 or more enemies or[[6]](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EA%B3%B5%ED%99%94%EA%B5%AD%EC%98%81%EC%9B%85#fn-6) It is said that one could receive it by accumulating special merits that could be used as propaganda material . As it was a difficult title to obtain, while some soldiers received it while alive, there were also many cases where it was awarded posthumously after death.
And at the time of the Korean War, there were soldiers who were awarded the title even though they were not in the North Korean army, and there were soldiers who were awarded the title among the Chinese troops who supported North Korea . According to the Chinese side, during the Korean War, a total of 12 Chinese soldiers were awarded the title of Heroes of the Republic.

## 2.Detail
In addition, when there is a national congratulation for a kind of 'enhancement of national prestige', the number of recipients other than soldiers increases rapidly. In December 2012, satellite A typical example is when as many as 201 scientists and those involved in satellite development/launch were simultaneously awarded after the successful launch of Kwangmyongsong-3 . After conducting the fourth underground nuclear test in January 2014, the same title was awarded to 200 officials.

## 2.Detail
Apart from such cases, it is very rare for this title to be conferred. In the case of female marathon runner Jung Sung -ok , who won the World Championships, she was originally scheduled to be awarded the title of Hero of Labor rather than Hero of the Republic . However, she received this title after enthusiastically praising Kim Il-sung and Kim Jong-il in an interview with foreign media after the competition, stating, "My victory is entirely thanks to our Great Leader and General." It is not as if she received the title of Hero merely for words like that.[[7]](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EA%B3%B5%ED%99%94%EA%B5%AD%EC%98%81%EC%9B%85#fn-7) To explain the full version, Kim Jong-il was moved by the fact that when asked about his feelings on winning, he said, “I recalled the image of the Great Leader calling out to me at the finish line, so I gave it my all until the end.” In addition to the title of Hero of the Republic, he was also awarded a Mercedes-Benz 400 and a luxury house in Pyongyang, and reportedly took home the entire $50,000 prize money.[[8]](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EA%B3%B5%ED%99%94%EA%B5%AD%EC%98%81%EC%9B%85#fn-8) Female judoka Kye Sun-hui, who won six gold medals in international competitions, is also a Labor Hero. Given that North Korea is obsessed with earning foreign currency prize money, it is highly unlikely that they would normally give the money to the athlete as is rather than confiscate it; thus, they gave her top-tier treatment with just a single word. However, a few years later, she reportedly confessed to the Chosun Sinbo , "I gained strength and won while looking at the wristwatch my lover personally put on my wristwatch," and it seems the Great Chairman of the National Defense Commission was completely fooled by words that were nothing more than lip service.

## 2.Detail
Recipients are supposed to receive the First Class Order of the National Flag at the same time, and like the Order of the Hero of the Soviet Union, it can be awarded to foreigners as well. At the same time, half-length statues are basically erected in the hometown or graveyard of the recipient, and it is not uncommon for there to be a school or factory named after the recipient . In the case of a military award, the name of the recipient and the hero title are added to the name of the unit to which the recipient belongs.[[9]](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EA%B3%B5%ED%99%94%EA%B5%AD%EC%98%81%EC%9B%85#fn-9)
It is the same with other North Korean medals, but negative perception continues to spread as the number of poor stars and other high-ranking people who receive awards for political considerations without much major is increasing . Maybe that's why, among the families of the Republic Hero + Honorary Soldier combo, there are cases where you have to resell 'beer tickets' to make a living...
It was once listed on eBay for $ 2,500 .

## 1.outline
north korea**This is the highest level title and decoration, and** its official name **is ‘Hero of the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea.’** It is easy to see that it is an imitation of the Hero of the Soviet Union , and was enacted on June 30, 1950, during the Korean War . At the time of enactment, he was considered a ‘Hero of the People’s Republic of Korea’.[[3]](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EA%B3%B5%ED%99%94%EA%B5%AD%EC%98%81%EC%9B%85#fn-3) The name was used. The first date the Hero of the Republic Medal was awarded was July 15, 1950, 15 days after it was established, and 12 people received it simultaneously.
The Hero of the Republic Medal has a star surrounded by a circle inside a gold five-pointed star similar to the Order of Kim Il Sung or Order of Kim Jong Il , and the star shape is the same as that of the Hero of the Soviet Union. When attaching it to clothes, connect metal pins with white lines on the left and right edges on a red background and attach it to the right side of the top (left side of the wearer).

## 2.Detail
> Article 1. The title of Hero of the People's Republic of Korea is the highest honor in the Democratic People's Republic of Korea and is awarded to those who have individually or collectively performed heroic feats in front of the state.  
>   
> Article 2. The title of Hero of the North Korean People's Republic is awarded by the Presidium of the Supreme People's Assembly of North Korea .  
>   
> Article 3. In addition to this title, the Hero of the People's Republic of Korea is awarded the First Class Gold Star Medal of the Order of the National Flag and a commendation from the Presidium of the Supreme People's Assembly of Korea.  
>   
> Article 4. If a person who has been awarded the title of Hero of the People's Republic of Korea has repeatedly performed heroic feats worthy of being titled a Hero of the People's Republic of Korea, a second gold star medal is awarded, and in addition, a meritorious service is awarded to the hero's hometown to praise and commemorate his heroic feat. erect a statue of In this case, a commendation from the Presidium of the Supreme People's Assembly of Korea is also awarded.  
>   
> Article 5. The annual pension for the First Class Order of the National Flag received simultaneously with the conferment of the title of Hero of the People's Republic of Korea shall be double the stipulated amount.  
>   
> Article 6. The title of Hero of the People's Republic of Korea is awarded even in the case of the death of a person who has performed heroic exploits .  
>   
> Article VII. A person who has been awarded the title of Hero of the People's Republic of Korea enjoys all privileges and rights according to the provisions of the Order of the National Flag of the 1st, 2nd and 3rd classes.  
>   
> Article 8. The title of Hero of the People's Republic of Korea can only be revoked by the Standing Committee of the Supreme People's Assembly of Korea.  
>   
> Article 9. The gold star medal is worn on the upper left chest.  
>   
>   
>   
> * * *  
>   
>   
> **Provisions for the title of Hero of the People's Republic of Korea**

## 2.Detail
The title of Hero of the Republic is mainly awarded to soldiers with special expertise. In addition to soldiers, it is also awarded to high-ranking politicians, railroad workers, security guards (police officers), etc., and very occasionally it is awarded to organizations, institutions, buildings, or objects other than people. . In addition, perhaps because it has the same characteristics as South Korea's Grand Order of Rose of Sharon, it was also awarded to leaders of North Korea's allies, such as Fidel Castro , Hosni Mubarak **,****Pol Pot** , **and Mengistu Haile Mariam** , but Putin, who visited North Korea in 2024, was awarded the Kim Il-sung Medal rather than the Hero of the Republic. It appears that the policy has changed.
According to North Korea, a total of 627 soldiers of the Korean People's Army were awarded the title of Hero of the Republic for their meritorious service during the Korean War.[[4]](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EA%B3%B5%ED%99%94%EA%B5%AD%EC%98%81%EC%9B%85#fn-4)[[5]](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EA%B3%B5%ED%99%94%EA%B5%AD%EC%98%81%EC%9B%85#fn-5) , generally, kill 50 or more enemies or[[6]](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EA%B3%B5%ED%99%94%EA%B5%AD%EC%98%81%EC%9B%85#fn-6) It is said that one could receive it by accumulating special merits that could be used as propaganda material . As it was a difficult title to obtain, while some soldiers received it while alive, there were also many cases where it was awarded posthumously after death.
And at the time of the Korean War, there were soldiers who were awarded the title even though they were not in the North Korean army, and there were soldiers who were awarded the title among the Chinese troops who supported North Korea . According to the Chinese side, during the Korean War, a total of 12 Chinese soldiers were awarded the title of Heroes of the Republic.

## 2.Detail
In addition, when there is a national congratulation for a kind of 'enhancement of national prestige', the number of recipients other than soldiers increases rapidly. In December 2012, satellite A typical example is when as many as 201 scientists and those involved in satellite development/launch were simultaneously awarded after the successful launch of Kwangmyongsong-3 . After conducting the fourth underground nuclear test in January 2014, the same title was awarded to 200 officials.

## 2.Detail
Apart from such cases, it is very rare for this title to be conferred. In the case of female marathon runner Jung Sung -ok , who won the World Championships, she was originally scheduled to be awarded the title of Hero of Labor rather than Hero of the Republic . However, she received this title after enthusiastically praising Kim Il-sung and Kim Jong-il in an interview with foreign media after the competition, stating, "My victory is entirely thanks to our Great Leader and General." It is not as if she received the title of Hero merely for words like that.[[7]](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EA%B3%B5%ED%99%94%EA%B5%AD%EC%98%81%EC%9B%85#fn-7) To explain the full version, Kim Jong-il was moved by the fact that when asked about his feelings on winning, he said, “I recalled the image of the Great Leader calling out to me at the finish line, so I gave it my all until the end.” In addition to the title of Hero of the Republic, he was also awarded a Mercedes-Benz 400 and a luxury house in Pyongyang, and reportedly took home the entire $50,000 prize money.[[8]](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EA%B3%B5%ED%99%94%EA%B5%AD%EC%98%81%EC%9B%85#fn-8) Female judoka Kye Sun-hui, who won six gold medals in international competitions, is also a Labor Hero. Given that North Korea is obsessed with earning foreign currency prize money, it is highly unlikely that they would normally give the money to the athlete as is rather than confiscate it; thus, they gave her top-tier treatment with just a single word. However, a few years later, she reportedly confessed to the Chosun Sinbo , "I gained strength and won while looking at the wristwatch my lover personally put on my wristwatch," and it seems the Great Chairman of the National Defense Commission was completely fooled by words that were nothing more than lip service.

## 2.Detail
Recipients are supposed to receive the First Class Order of the National Flag at the same time, and like the Order of the Hero of the Soviet Union, it can be awarded to foreigners as well. At the same time, half-length statues are basically erected in the hometown or graveyard of the recipient, and it is not uncommon for there to be a school or factory named after the recipient . In the case of a military award, the name of the recipient and the hero title are added to the name of the unit to which the recipient belongs.[[9]](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EA%B3%B5%ED%99%94%EA%B5%AD%EC%98%81%EC%9B%85#fn-9)
It is the same with other North Korean medals, but negative perception continues to spread as the number of poor stars and other high-ranking people who receive awards for political considerations without much major is increasing . Maybe that's why, among the families of the Republic Hero + Honorary Soldier combo, there are cases where you have to resell 'beer tickets' to make a living...
It was once listed on eBay for $ 2,500 .

## 1.outline
north korea**This is the highest level title and decoration, and** its official name **is ‘Hero of the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea.’** It is easy to see that it is an imitation of the Hero of the Soviet Union , and was enacted on June 30, 1950, during the Korean War . At the time of enactment, he was considered a ‘Hero of the People’s Republic of Korea’.[[3]](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EA%B3%B5%ED%99%94%EA%B5%AD%EC%98%81%EC%9B%85#fn-3) The name was used. The first date the Hero of the Republic Medal was awarded was July 15, 1950, 15 days after it was established, and 12 people received it simultaneously.
The Hero of the Republic Medal has a star surrounded by a circle inside a gold five-pointed star similar to the Order of Kim Il Sung or Order of Kim Jong Il , and the star shape is the same as that of the Hero of the Soviet Union. When attaching it to clothes, connect metal pins with white lines on the left and right edges on a red background and attach it to the right side of the top (left side of the wearer).

## 2.Detail
> Article 1. The title of Hero of the People's Republic of Korea is the highest honor in the Democratic People's Republic of Korea and is awarded to those who have individually or collectively performed heroic feats in front of the state.  
>   
> Article 2. The title of Hero of the North Korean People's Republic is awarded by the Presidium of the Supreme People's Assembly of North Korea .  
>   
> Article 3. In addition to this title, the Hero of the People's Republic of Korea is awarded the First Class Gold Star Medal of the Order of the National Flag and a commendation from the Presidium of the Supreme People's Assembly of Korea.  
>   
> Article 4. If a person who has been awarded the title of Hero of the People's Republic of Korea has repeatedly performed heroic feats worthy of being titled a Hero of the People's Republic of Korea, a second gold star medal is awarded, and in addition, a meritorious service is awarded to the hero's hometown to praise and commemorate his heroic feat. erect a statue of In this case, a commendation from the Presidium of the Supreme People's Assembly of Korea is also awarded.  
>   
> Article 5. The annual pension for the First Class Order of the National Flag received simultaneously with the conferment of the title of Hero of the People's Republic of Korea shall be double the stipulated amount.  
>   
> Article 6. The title of Hero of the People's Republic of Korea is awarded even in the case of the death of a person who has performed heroic exploits .  
>   
> Article VII. A person who has been awarded the title of Hero of the People's Republic of Korea enjoys all privileges and rights according to the provisions of the Order of the National Flag of the 1st, 2nd and 3rd classes.  
>   
> Article 8. The title of Hero of the People's Republic of Korea can only be revoked by the Standing Committee of the Supreme People's Assembly of Korea.  
>   
> Article 9. The gold star medal is worn on the upper left chest.  
>

## 2.Detail
The title of Hero of the Republic is mainly awarded to soldiers with special expertise. In addition to soldiers, it is also awarded to high-ranking politicians, railroad workers, security guards (police officers), etc., and very occasionally it is awarded to organizations, institutions, buildings, or objects other than people. . In addition, perhaps because it has the same characteristics as South Korea's Grand Order of Rose of Sharon, it was also awarded to leaders of North Korea's allies, such as Fidel Castro , Hosni Mubarak **,****Pol Pot** , **and Mengistu Haile Mariam** , but Putin, who visited North Korea in 2024, was awarded the Kim Il-sung Medal rather than the Hero of the Republic. It appears that the policy has changed.
According to North Korea, a total of 627 soldiers of the Korean People's Army were awarded the title of Hero of the Republic for their meritorious service during the Korean War.[[4]](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EA%B3%B5%ED%99%94%EA%B5%AD%EC%98%81%EC%9B%85#fn-4)[[5]](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EA%B3%B5%ED%99%94%EA%B5%AD%EC%98%81%EC%9B%85#fn-5) , generally, kill 50 or more enemies or[[6]](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EA%B3%B5%ED%99%94%EA%B5%AD%EC%98%81%EC%9B%85#fn-6) It is said that one could receive it by accumulating special merits that could be used as propaganda material . As it was a difficult title to obtain, while some soldiers received it while alive, there were also many cases where it was awarded posthumously after death.
And at the time of the Korean War, there were soldiers who were awarded the title even though they were not in the North Korean army, and there were soldiers who were awarded the title among the Chinese troops who supported North Korea . According to the Chinese side, during the Korean War, a total of 12 Chinese soldiers were awarded the title of Heroes of the Republic.

## 2.Detail
In addition, when there is a national congratulation for a kind of 'enhancement of national prestige', the number of recipients other than soldiers increases rapidly. In December 2012, satellite A typical example is when as many as 201 scientists and those involved in satellite development/launch were simultaneously awarded after the successful launch of Kwangmyongsong-3 . After conducting the fourth underground nuclear test in January 2014, the same title was awarded to 200 officials.

## 2.Detail
Apart from such cases, it is very rare for this title to be conferred. In the case of female marathon runner Jung Sung -ok , who won the World Championships, she was originally scheduled to be awarded the title of Hero of Labor rather than Hero of the Republic . However, she received this title after enthusiastically praising Kim Il-sung and Kim Jong-il in an interview with foreign media after the competition, stating, "My victory is entirely thanks to our Great Leader and General." It is not as if she received the title of Hero merely for words like that.[[7]](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EA%B3%B5%ED%99%94%EA%B5%AD%EC%98%81%EC%9B%85#fn-7) To explain the full version, Kim Jong-il was moved by the fact that when asked about his feelings on winning, he said, “I recalled the image of the Great Leader calling out to me at the finish line, so I gave it my all until the end.” In addition to the title of Hero of the Republic, he was also awarded a Mercedes-Benz 400 and a luxury house in Pyongyang, and reportedly took home the entire $50,000 prize money.[[8]](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EA%B3%B5%ED%99%94%EA%B5%AD%EC%98%81%EC%9B%85#fn-8) Female judoka Kye Sun-hui, who won six gold medals in international competitions, is also a Labor Hero. Given that North Korea is obsessed with earning foreign currency prize money, it is highly unlikely that they would normally give the money to the athlete as is rather than confiscate it; thus, they gave her top-tier treatment with just a single word. However, a few years later, she reportedly confessed to the Chosun Sinbo , "I gained strength and won while looking at the wristwatch my lover personally put on my wristwatch," and it seems the Great Chairman of the National Defense Commission was completely fooled by words that were nothing more than lip service.

## 2.Detail
Recipients are supposed to receive the First Class Order of the National Flag at the same time, and like the Order of the Hero of the Soviet Union, it can be awarded to foreigners as well. At the same time, half-length statues are basically erected in the hometown or graveyard of the recipient, and it is not uncommon for there to be a school or factory named after the recipient . In the case of a military award, the name of the recipient and the hero title are added to the name of the unit to which the recipient belongs.[[9]](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EA%B3%B5%ED%99%94%EA%B5%AD%EC%98%81%EC%9B%85#fn-9)
It is the same with other North Korean medals, but negative perception continues to spread as the number of poor stars and other high-ranking people who receive awards for political considerations without much major is increasing . Maybe that's why, among the families of the Republic Hero + Honorary Soldier combo, there are cases where you have to resell 'beer tickets' to make a living...
It was once listed on eBay for $ 2,500 .

## International honours and recognition
[edit]
*   In July 1999, Bachchan was named the "Greatest Star of stage or screen of the Millennium" by BBC online poll where he defeated many Hollywood legends such as Alec Guinness, Marlon Brando, Laurence Olivier and Charlie Chaplin.[[197]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Amitabh_Bachchan#cite_note-197)  
*   In 2001, he was ranked as the "Most Powerful Indian Film Star" by _Forbes_.[[198]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Amitabh_Bachchan#cite_note-198)  
*   On 10 September 2001 he was awarded the "Actor of the Century" award at the Alexandria International Film Festival. Egyptian Minister of Culture Farouk Hosni presented Bachchan with the award in recognition of his contribution to international cinema.[[199]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Amitabh_Bachchan#cite_note-199)  
*   On 14 March 2003, he was conferred with the honorary citizenship of the French town of Deauville at the fifth edition of the Asian film festival. An honour earlier bestowed on only two people, Queen Elizabeth II and the Soviet space hero, Yuri Gagarin.[[200]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Amitabh_Bachchan#cite_note-200)  
*   In October 2003, he was conferred with the Medal of Honour of Morocco, given to him by King Mohammed at the Marrakech International Film Festival.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Amitabh_Bachchan#cite_note-Marrakech-21)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Amitabh_Bachchan#cite_note-timesofindia.indiatimes.com-22)

## International honours and recognition
*   In October 2003, _Time_ magazine dubbed Bachchan as "the Undisputed Godfather of Bollywood".[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Amitabh_Bachchan#cite_note-Perry-23) He was also featured in its list of Bollywood's Brightest Stars.[[201]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Amitabh_Bachchan#cite_note-201)  
*   In April 2005, The Walter Reade Theater of Lincoln Center in New York honored Amitabh Bachchan with a special tribute, retrospective—titled "Amitabh Bachchan: The Biggest Film Star in the World".[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Amitabh_Bachchan#cite_note-Saltz-24)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Amitabh_Bachchan#cite_note-thedailybeast.com/newsweek-25) The tribute also included "An Evening with Amitabh Bachchan", a live appearance by Bachchan hosted at the Lincoln Center's Alice Tully Hall.[[202]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Amitabh_Bachchan#cite_note-An_Evening_with_Amitabh_Bachchan-202)  
*   He was honoured along with actors and directors from Hollywood at an International Film Festival in Rabat, Morocco.[[203]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Amitabh_Bachchan#cite_note-Joining_the_ranks-203)  
*   In the weekend of 16 and 17 June June 2007, the British Academy of Film and Television Arts (BAFTA) hosts a Bachchan spectacular retrospective to honour Bachchan's stellar career. The Chairman of BAFTA ended the event by announcing Bachchan as an honorary Life-Time member of BAFTA.[[204]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Amitabh_Bachchan#cite_note-204)

## International honours and recognition
*   On 22 November 2007 he was honoured by the London Mayor Ken Livingstone with "The Visit London Special Award for Outstanding Achievement" for his contribution to Indian cinema in the last 30 years.[[205]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Amitabh_Bachchan#cite_note-205)  
*   On 15 January 2009, Le Salon du Cinema (Cinema Fair) in Paris paid tribute to Indian Cinema for their new edition, with Bachchan being the guest of honour. He also launched a retrospective of his films.[[206]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Amitabh_Bachchan#cite_note-206)  
*   On 31 January 2009, he was honoured with the World Economic Forum's Crystal Award at Davos for his contribution to the world of art.[[207]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Amitabh_Bachchan#cite_note-207)  
*   In 2009, the Tehran Film Festival has invited Bachchan to receive the Lifetime Achievement Award.[[208]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Amitabh_Bachchan#cite_note-208)  
*   In December 2009, he was honoured with a Lifetime Achievement Award at the Dubai International Film Festival for his outstanding contribution to cinema.[[209]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Amitabh_Bachchan#cite_note-209)  
*   In December 2009, he was honoured with the 8th Asian Film Cultural Award for his contribution to cinema for 40 years.[[210]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Amitabh_Bachchan#cite_note-210)

## [PDF page 6]
IOWA:  State  Auditor  Rob  Sand  (D)  flipped  the  Iowa  governor’s  office,  defeating  businessman  Zach  Lahn  (R)  
55.5%  to  44.5%.  Sand,  the  only  Democrat  holding  statewide  office  before  the  election,  is  the  first  Democrat  
elected  governor  since  Chet  Culver  in  2006  and  succeeds  Governor  Kim  Reynolds  (R),  who  did  not  seek  
reelection.  His  win  ends  the  Republican  trifecta  in  place  since  2017.  Democrats  also  flipped  the  open  U.S.  
Senate seat, as state Representative Josh Turek (D) defeated U.S. Representative Ashley Hinson (R) 51% to 46%  
for the first Democratic Senate win in Iowa since 2008. Sand ran roughly five points ahead of Turek.
KANSAS: In the race to succeed term-limited Governor Laura Kelly (D), state Senator Cindy Holscher (D) leads  
Senate President Ty Masterson (R) 50.3% to 49.7%, ahead by nearly 7,000 votes out of more than 1 million cast. A  
Masterson win would flip the seat to Republicans. As of November 6, 12:04 PM ET.
MAINE: Former Maine House Speaker Hannah Pingree (D) won the three-way race for governor with 55% of the  
vote, defeating former U.S. Assistant Secretary of State Bobby Charles (R), who received 37%, and independent  
state Senator Rick Bennett, who received 8%. Pingree, the daughter of U.S. Representative Chellie Pingree (D),  
emerged from a crowded Democratic primary and succeeds term-limited Governor Janet Mills (D), keeping the  
seat in Democratic control.

## [PDF page 6]
MARYLAND: Governor Wes Moore (D), the state’s first Black governor, won a second term by defeating former  
Delegate Dan Cox (R) 63% to 33% in a rematch of their 2022 race. Moore’s reelection keeps Democrats in full  
control of Maryland’s state government.
MASSACHUSETTS:  Governor  Maura  Healey  (D)  won  a  second  term,  defeating  former  Abiomed  CEO  Mike  
Minogue (R) 63% to 33%. Healey, who served two terms as attorney general before becoming the state’s first  
female governor, will continue to work with Democratic supermajorities in both chambers of the Legislature.
PAGE  04

## [PDF page 7]
Governors
MICHIGAN: Secretary of State Jocelyn Benson (D) defeated U.S. Representative John James (R) 55% to 44% to  
succeed term-limited Governor Gretchen Whitmer (D), giving Democrats three consecutive Michigan governor’s  
race wins for the first time since 1960. Benson ran ahead of the top of the federal ticket: former Detroit health  
director Abdul El-Sayed (D) won the open U.S. Senate seat over former U.S. Representative Mike Rogers (R) by a  
narrower  53%  to  46%.  With  Democrats  holding  the  state  Senate  and  flipping  the  state  House,  Benson’s  win  
restores the Democratic trifecta the party lost when Republicans took the House in 2024.
MINNESOTA: U.S. Senator Amy Klobuchar (DFL) will be Minnesota’s first female governor after defeating House  
Speaker  Lisa  Demuth  (R)  56%  to  42%.  Klobuchar,  who  has  served  in  the  U.S.  Senate  since  2007  and  ran  for  
president  in  2020,  succeeds  Governor  Tim  Walz  (DFL),  the  2024  Democratic  vice-presidential  nominee,  who  
dropped his bid for a third term in January. Klobuchar’s U.S. Senate seat will be filled by appointment.
NEBRASKA: Governor Jim Pillen (R) won a second term over former state Senator Lynne Walz (D) 49% to 45%,  
keeping Nebraska’s governorship Republican for an eighth straight election. Pillen will continue working with a  
Republican-aligned majority in the nonpartisan, one-chamber Legislature.

## [PDF page 7]
NEW HAMPSHIRE: Governor Kelly Ayotte (R) won reelection over former Executive Councilor Cinde Warmington  
(D) 51% to 47%, even as many of the same voters backed Democrats for federal office. U.S. Representative Chris  
Pappas (D) won the open U.S. Senate seat over former U.S. Senator John E. Sununu (R) 56% to 42%, a swing of  
roughly 18 points between the two statewide races. New Hampshire has now elected Republican governors six  
straight times, dating to Chris Sununu’s 2016 win, even though it voted for former Vice President Kamala Harris in  
2024.
NEW MEXICO: Former U.S. Interior Secretary Deb Haaland (D) became the first Native American woman elected  
governor of any state, defeating former Rio Rancho Mayor Gregg Hull (R) 57% to 43%. Haaland, a former U.S.  
representative,  succeeds  term-limited  Governor  Michelle  Lujan  Grisham  (D)  and  will  be  New  Mexico’s  third  
consecutive female governor.
NEW YORK: Governor Kathy Hochul (D), the state’s first female governor, won a second full term by defeating  
Nassau  County  Executive  Bruce  Blakeman  (R)  63%  to  37%,  the  widest  margin  in  a  New  York  governor’s  race  
since 2018. Hochul took office in 2021 after Governor Andrew Cuomo resigned and was elected to her first full  
term in 2022. Blakeman earned President Trump’s endorsement after U.S. Representative Elise Stefanik left the  
race, but Republicans have not won a statewide race in New York since Governor George Pataki’s reelection in  
2002. Hochul will again work with Democratic majorities in both chambers of the Legislature.

## [PDF page 7]
OKLAHOMA:  Former  state  Budget  Secretary  Mike  Mazzei  (R),  also  a  former  state  senator,  won  the  open  
governor’s  race  over  House  Minority  Leader  Cyndi  Munson  (D)  52%  to  46%.  Mazzei  succeeds  term-limited  
Governor Kevin Stitt (R). Republicans have held every statewide office in Oklahoma since the 2010 election.

## [PDF page 15]
Other Statewide Races
LIEUTENANT GOVERNORS  
Thirty-one lieutenant governor seats were on the ballot this year, including Arizona’s first-ever election for the  
office,  which  voters  created  in  2022.  The  other  30  were  split  evenly  between  the  parties,  and  Republicans  
entered Election Day holding 24 lieutenant governorships nationally to Democrats’ 20. Democrats gained a net  
six  seats,  flipping  Georgia,  Iowa,  Nevada,  Ohio,  Texas  and  Vermont,  and  also  won  Arizona’s  new  office  on  
Governor  Katie  Hobbs’  ticket.  Three  of  those  flips  came  at  the  expense  of  incumbents.  In  Texas,  state  
Representative Vikki Goodwin (D) unseated Lieutenant Governor Dan Patrick (R); in Nevada, Assemblywoman  
Sandra  Jauregui  (D)  defeated  Lieutenant  Governor  Stavros  Anthony  (R);  and  in  Vermont,  former  Lieutenant  
Governor  Molly  Gray  defeated  Lieutenant  Governor  John  Rodgers  (R).  Democrats  now  hold  26  lieutenant  
governorships to Republicans’ 17, with races in Alaska and Kansas, where the lieutenant governor runs on a  
joint ticket with the governor, still uncalled.

## [PDF page 15]
SECRETARIES OF STATE  
Twenty-six secretary of state offices were on the ballot this year, 13 held by each party. In 23 of those states, the  
secretary of state is the chief election official. Republicans entered Election Day holding 25 offices nationally to  
Democrats’  22,  so  Democrats  needed  a  net  gain  of  two  seats  to  win  a  majority.  They  gained  three,  flipping  
Georgia, Indiana and Ohio, and held every seat they defended, including the battleground offices in Arizona,  
Michigan, Nevada and Wisconsin. In Georgia, former Judge Penny Brown Reynolds (D) will become the state’s  
first Black secretary of state. Democrats now hold a 25-21 majority, with Kansas, where Pat Proctor (R) leads  
48.4% to 47.4%, still uncalled.
STATE SCHOOL SUPERINTENDENTS  
Twelve states elect their school superintendents, and seven held those elections this year: Arizona, California,  
Georgia, Idaho, Oklahoma, South Carolina and Wyoming. When the same seven offices were last on the ballot  
in  2022,  Republicans  swept  all  six  partisan  contests,  while  Democrats  held  California’s  nonpartisan  office.  
California’s race carried lower stakes this year, since Governor Gavin Newsom and legislative leaders moved  
most  of  the  office’s  authority  to  a  gubernatorial  appointee  starting  next  year.  In  most  other  states,  the  chief  
school officer is appointed by the governor or the state board of education, so open governor’s races in states  
such as Iowa, Maine, Minnesota, New Mexico, Ohio and Tennessee will also bring new education leadership.

## [PDF page 15]
Democrats flipped two offices. In Georgia, they unseated the Republican incumbent as part of their sweep of  
statewide  offices  there.  In  Arizona,  former  Glendale  Community  College  President  Teresa  Leyba  Ruiz  (D)  
defeated  State  Treasurer  Kimberly  Yee  (R)  53%  to  47%,  becoming  the  first  Latina  elected  to  lead  the  state’s  
public  schools.  Yee  had  ousted  Superintendent  Tom  Horne  (R)  in  the  July  primary.  Republicans  held  the  
remaining offices. Superintendent Debbie Critchfield (R) won a second term in Idaho, and Superintendent Ellen  
Weaver (R) was reelected in South Carolina. In Oklahoma, longtime educator Robert Franklin (R), a registered  
Democrat  until  2022,  won  the  open  seat  on  a  promise  to  depoliticize  the  office  after  the  tenure  of  former  
Superintendent  Ryan  Walters  (R).  In  Wyoming,  former  House  Speaker  Steve  Harshman  (R)  defeated  Ana  
Cordova  (D)  75%  to  25%  for  the  seat  left  open  by  Superintendent  Megan  Degenfelder  (R),  who  lost  the  
Republican primary for governor. Democrats will now hold two of the six partisan offices on the ballot, up from  
none.

## [PDF page 16]
Other Statewide Races
STATE AUDITORS  
Fourteen state auditor offices were on the ballot this year, six held by Democrats and eight by Republicans.  
Before the election, Republicans held 23 auditor offices nationally to Democrats’ 14, with one unaffiliated. In  
Ohio, Secretary of State Frank LaRose (R) won the open seat, leading Annette Blackwell (D) 50.8% to 49.2% with  
98% reporting when Blackwell conceded. In Iowa, the race remains uncalled, with Taylor Wettach (D) leading  
Lieutenant Governor Chris Cournoyer (R) 50.2% to 49.8%, a margin of roughly 5,500 votes, for the seat vacated  
by Governor-elect Rob Sand (D). If Wettach’s lead holds, neither seat will change parties.
STATE PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSIONERS  
Nine  states  held  public  service  commissioner  elections  this  year:  Alabama,  Arizona,  Georgia,  Louisiana,  
Montana,  Nebraska,  North  Dakota,  Oklahoma  and  South  Dakota.  Republicans  entered  with  majorities  on  all  
nine commissions. The fight centered on Georgia, where Democrats unseated two Republican commissioners  
in 2025 amid voter frustration over rising power bills and data centers. This year, Democrats won both seats on  
the  ballot,  as  Commissioner  Peter  Hubbard  (D)  defeated  former  Commissioner  Fitz  Johnson  (R)  and  Shelia  
Edwards  (D)  flipped  the  open  District  5  seat,  giving  Democrats  a  3-2  majority  for  the  first  time  in  decades.  
Georgia was the only commission to change party control.

## [PDF page 16]
In Arizona, Democrats ended single-party control of the Corporation Commission. Campaigning on data center  
transparency and utility costs, Clara Pratte (D) and Jonathon Hill (D) defeated Commissioner Kevin Thompson  
(R) and state Representative Ralph Heap (R), leaving Republicans with a 3-2 majority. Pratte, a member of the  
Navajo Nation, becomes the first Indigenous woman elected statewide in Arizona. Louisiana moved the other  
way. Republicans won both open seats, and Caddo Parish Commissioner John Atkins (R) flipped District 5, held  
by Democrats since its creation in 1974, expanding the Republican majority to 4-1.
Republicans held their ground elsewhere. In Alabama, Matt Gentry (R) and Jim Zeigler (R) each won with about  
55%, a closer margin than usual for the state. In Oklahoma, state Representative Brad Boles (R), who sponsored  
the state’s data center law, won the open seat. Republicans also swept the seats on the ballot in North Dakota,  
South  Dakota  and  Montana,  where  the  commission  remains  all-Republican,  as  it  has  been  since  2012.  
Nebraska’s open District 2 remains uncalled, as state Senator Wendy DeBoer (D) seeks to return a Democrat to  
the all-Republican commission against Dennis McCann (R).

## [PDF page 16]
AGRICULTURAL COMMISSIONERS  
Seven states elected agriculture commissioners or their equivalent on November 3. Democrats flipped Texas  
and Georgia, and Republicans held the other five. In Texas, rancher Clayton Tucker (D) defeated Nate Sheets (R)  
51% to 47%, becoming the state’s first Democratic agriculture commissioner in nearly 40 years. Sheets had  
ousted  three-term  Commissioner  Sid  Miller  (R)  in  the  March  primary.  In  Georgia,  Katherine  Juhan-Arnold  (D)  
unseated  one-term  Commissioner  Tyler  Harper  (R)  54%  to  46%.  Republicans  held  the  remaining  offices.  
Commissioner Wilton Simpson (R) won reelection in Florida with 51%, Secretary of Agriculture Mike Naig (R)  
won  a  third  full  term  in  Iowa,  and  Commissioner  Doug  Goehring  (R)  was  reelected  in  North  Dakota.  Cody  
Simpson  (R)  won  South  Carolina’s  open  seat  52%  to  46%,  and  Corey  Hill  (R)  won  Alabama’s  open  seat,  
defeating former Commissioner Ron Sparks (D).
PAGE 14

## [PDF page 17]
State Legislatures
Voters in 46 states filled 6,139 legislative seats across 88 chambers on November 3. Democrats  
flipped  at  least  10  chambers  and  lead  in  two  more,  based  on  unofficial  results.  Republicans  
entered the night holding 57 of 99 chambers to Democrats’ 39. If current results hold, Democrats  
would control 51 chambers to Republicans’ 46, the first Democratic chamber edge in more than a  
decade.
ALASKA: Alaska is the only state where both legislative chambers are run by bipartisan coalitions  
of Democrats, independents and moderate Republicans, even though Republicans hold the most  
seats in each. Before the election, the House coalition held the bare minimum of 21 seats needed  
to  govern,  while  the  Senate  coalition  held  a  wider  14-6  edge.  Results  show  the  coalitions  
potentially expanding their control: Democrats and independents lead in 23 of 40 House races  
and have flipped at least two Republican-held seats, while no member of the 14-member Senate  
coalition trails a conservative challenger. Many races are headed to ranked-choice tabulation, so  
final results are not expected until later this month. If the coalitions hold and Democrat Jonathan  
Kreiss-Tomkins wins the uncalled governor’s race, Alaska would have its first governor in years  
working with a Legislature led by allies rather than opponents.
ARIZONA: Republicans held narrow majorities in both chambers before the election, 33-27 in the  
House and 17-13 in the Senate. Democrats flipped the Senate, which they last controlled in 1992,  
and lead in 37 of 60 House races, putting them on track to win the chamber for the first time since  
1966. If the House result holds, Governor Katie Hobbs (D) would begin her second term with the  
state’s first Democratic trifecta in 60 years. The House may not be called for several days while  
ballots are still being counted.

## [PDF page 17]
COLORADO: Democrats already held a trifecta in Colorado and expanded their House majority to  
two-thirds. Paired with Governor-elect Phil Weiser (D), the new supermajority brings Democrats  
closer to the two-thirds needed in both chambers to refer constitutional amendments to voters.
FLORIDA: Republicans kept control of both chambers but lost the supermajorities they had held  
in each, as Democrats flipped at least 16 House seats and a Senate seat (final counts are still  
being  tabulated).  With  Governor-elect  Byron  Donalds  (R)  in  office,  the  change  does  not  affect  
vetoes, but Republicans will now need Democratic votes for anything requiring a two-thirds vote.
GEORGIA: Republicans have controlled both chambers of the General Assembly for more than  
two  decades,  holding  the  House  100-80  after  the  2024  election.  Governor-elect  Keisha  Lance  
Bottoms’  (D)  win  broke  the  Republican  trifecta  in  place  since  2005.  Democrats  have  also  
declared a majority in the House, which they have not held since 2002, though the chamber has  
not been called. Republicans kept control of the Senate but lost their supermajority.
PAGE 15

## [PDF page 18]
State Legislatures
IOWA: Republicans have held a trifecta in Iowa since 2017, along with exactly two-thirds of both  
chambers, the threshold needed to override a veto. Governor-elect Rob Sand’s (D) win ended the  
trifecta, and Democrats broke the Republican supermajority in the House. Because veto overrides  
in  Iowa  require  two-thirds  of  both  chambers,  Sand’s  vetoes  will  hold  even  though  Republicans  
kept their majorities.
KANSAS:  Kansas  had  divided  government  before  the  election,  with  Republicans  holding  
supermajorities of 88-37 in the House and 31-9 in the Senate and routinely overriding Governor  
Laura Kelly (D). Democrats broke the House supermajority, the only chamber on the ballot. If state  
Senator  Cindy  Holscher  (D)  holds  her  narrow  lead  in  the  uncalled  governor’s  race,  her  vetoes  
would be far harder to override than Kelly’s.
MICHIGAN: Control of the Legislature was split before the election, with Republicans holding the  
House 58-52 and Democrats holding the Senate 20-18. Democrats held the Senate and flipped the  
House, and with Governor-elect Jocelyn Benson (D), the party regains the trifecta it lost after the  
2024 election.
MINNESOTA: The House has been tied at 67-67 under a power-sharing agreement, and the DFL  
held the Senate 34-33. The DFL won the House outright and held the Senate, returning the party to  
a trifecta with Governor-elect Amy Klobuchar (DFL).
MISSOURI:  Republicans  kept  control  of  both  chambers,  but  Democrats  ended  their  
supermajorities in each, picking up at least 15 House seats and 2 Senate seats. Governor Mike  
Kehoe (R) still works with Republican majorities, but measures requiring a two-thirds vote, such as  
emergency clauses that let laws take effect immediately, will now need Democratic support.

## [PDF page 18]
NEVADA: Democrats controlled both chambers before the election but were each one seat short  
of the two-thirds needed to override Governor Joe Lombardo’s (R) vetoes. Governor-elect Aaron  
Ford’s (D) win gives Democrats a trifecta for the first time since 2023, and the party also won a  
two-thirds supermajority in the Assembly. Nevada requires a two-thirds vote in each chamber to  
raise taxes, so Democrats will still need Republican support in the Senate to pass any revenue  
increase.
NEW HAMPSHIRE: Before the election, Republicans held the 400-member House by more than 30  
seats and the Senate 16-8. Democrats flipped both chambers, ending the Republican trifecta even  
as Governor Kelly Ayotte (R) won reelection, and now control the full General Court for the first  
time  since  2018.  Democrats  won  a  two-thirds  majority  in  the  House,  while  one  Senate  race  
remains within recount range.
NEW  YORK:  Democrats  expanded  their  Senate  majority  to  a  supermajority,  strengthening  their  
hand alongside Governor Kathy Hochul (D).
NORTH  CAROLINA:  Before  the  election,  Republicans  held  the  Senate  30-20,  exactly  enough  to  
override Governor Josh Stein’s (D) vetoes, and the House 71-47, one seat short. Democrats flipped  
the House for the first time since 2010 and broke the Senate supermajority, so Stein’s vetoes will  
now hold in both chambers after two years of overrides.
PAGE 16

## [PDF page 19]
State Legislatures
OHIO: Republicans held a trifecta before the election, with veto-proof majorities of 65-34 in the  
House  and  24-9  in  the  Senate.  Governor-elect  Amy  Acton’s  (D)  win  ended  the  trifecta,  and  
Democrats broke the House supermajority. Because Ohio requires three-fifths of both chambers  
to override a veto, Acton’s vetoes will hold, although Republicans kept their supermajority in the  
Senate.
PENNSYLVANIA: Before the election, Democrats held the House 103-100, and Republicans held  
the Senate 27-23. In one of the night’s most significant results, Democrats held the House and  
flipped the Senate, giving Pennsylvania a trifecta for the first time since 1993.
SOUTH  CAROLINA:  Republicans  kept  control  of  both  chambers,  but  Democrats  broke  the  
Republican supermajority in the House. With Governor-elect Alan Wilson (R) in office, the practical  
effect is limited to measures requiring a two-thirds vote.
TEXAS: Republicans held the House 88-62 before the election. Democrats flipped the chamber,  
winning control for the first time since the 2002 election, while Republicans held the Senate 19-12.  
With  Governor-elect  Gina  Hinojosa’s  (D)  win  breaking  the  Republican  trifecta,  Texas  now  has  
divided government.
VERMONT: Republicans made surprising gains in 2024, breaking Democratic supermajorities in  
both  chambers  after  Governor  Phil  Scott  (R)  invested  considerable  time  and  resources  in  
legislative  races.  This  year,  Democrats  won  back  two-thirds  majorities  in  both  the  House  and  
Senate.  Scott  won  a  record  sixth  term,  but  Democrats  will  now  have  the  votes  to  override  his  
vetoes, the most consequential supermajority change of the night.

## [PDF page 19]
WISCONSIN:  Republicans  held  the  Assembly  54-45  and  the  Senate  18-15  before  the  election,  
under maps first used in 2024. Democrats flipped both chambers for the first time since 2010, and  
with Governor-elect David Crowley (D), the party has its first trifecta in 16 years.
KEIFFER MITCHELL JR. · BGR Vice President
“Elections set the direction, however, governing happens in the details. The results from the  
Midterm Elections will reshape the relationship between the states and Washington. Expect  
state legislatures to lead on affordability, energy costs, workforce, and technology policy.”

keeping Nebraska’s governorship Republican for an eighth straight election. Pillen will continue working with a  
Republican-aligned majority in the nonpartisan, one-chamber Legislature.

NEW HAMPSHIRE: Governor Kelly Ayotte (R) won reelection over former Executive Councilor Cinde Warmington  
(D) 51% to 47%, even as many of the same voters backed Democrats for federal office. U.S. Representative Chris  
Pappas (D) won the open U.S. Senate seat over former U.S. Senator John E. Sununu (R) 56% to 42%, a swing of

Other Statewide Races
LIEUTENANT GOVERNORS  
Thirty-one lieutenant governor seats were on the ballot this year, including Arizona’s first-ever election for the  
office,  which  voters  created  in  2022.  The  other  30  were  split  evenly  between  the  parties,  and  Republicans  
entered Election Day holding 24 lieutenant governorships nationally to Democrats’ 20. Democrats gained a net  
six  seats,  flipping  Georgia,  Iowa,  Nevada,  Ohio,  Texas  and  Vermont,  and  also  won  Arizona’s  new  office  on  
Governor  Katie  Hobbs’  ticket.  Three  of  those  flips  came  at  the  expense  of  incumbents.  In  Texas,  state  
Representative Vikki Goodwin (D) unseated Lieutenant Governor Dan Patrick (R); in Nevada, Assemblywoman  
Sandra  Jauregui  (D)  defeated  Lieutenant  Governor  Stavros  Anthony  (R);  and  in  Vermont,  former  Lieutenant  
Governor  Molly  Gray  defeated  Lieutenant  Governor  John  Rodgers  (R).  Democrats  now  hold  26  lieutenant  
governorships to Republicans’ 17, with races in Alaska and Kansas, where the lieutenant governor runs on a  
joint ticket with the governor, still uncalled.
texts.30:
## [PDF page 15]
SECRETARIES OF STATE  
Twenty-six secretary of state offices were on the ballot this year, 13 held by each party. In 23 of those states, the  
secretary of state is the chief election official. Republicans entered Election Day holding 25 offices nationally to  
Democrats’  22,  so  Democrats  needed  a  net  gain  of  two  seats  to  win  a  majority.  They  gained  three,  flipping  
Georgia, Indiana and Ohio, and held every seat they defended, including the battleground offices in Arizona,  
Michigan, Nevada and Wisconsin. In Georgia, former Judge Penny Brown Reynolds (D) will become the state’s  
first Black secretary of state. Democrats now hold a 25-21 majority, with Kansas, where Pat Proctor (R) leads  
48.4% to 47.4%, still uncalled.
STATE SCHOOL SUPERINTENDENTS  
Twelve states elect their school superintendents, and seven held those elections this year: Arizona, California,  
Georgia, Idaho, Oklahoma, South Carolina and Wyoming. When the same seven offices were last on the ballot  
in  2022,  Republicans  swept  all  six  partisan  contests,  while  Democrats  held  California’s  nonpartisan  office.  
California’s race carried lower stakes this year, since Governor Gavin Newsom and legislative leaders moved  
most  of  the  office’s  authority  to  a  gubernatorial  appointee  starting  next  year.  In  most  other  states,  the  chief  
school officer is appointed by the governor or the state board of education, so open governor’s races in states  
such as Iowa, Maine, Minnesota, New Mexico, Ohio and Tennessee will also bring new education leadership.

## [PDF page 15]
Democrats flipped two offices. In Georgia, they unseated the Republican incumbent as part of their sweep of  
statewide  offices  there.  In  Arizona,  former  Glendale  Community  College  President  Teresa  Leyba  Ruiz  (D)  
defeated  State  Treasurer  Kimberly  Yee  (R)  53%  to  47%,  becoming  the  first  Latina  elected  to  lead  the  state’s  
public  schools.  Yee  had  ousted  Superintendent  Tom  Horne  (R)  in  the  July  primary.  Republicans  held  the  
remaining offices. Superintendent Debbie Critchfield (R) won a second term in Idaho, and Superintendent Ellen  
Weaver (R) was reelected in South Carolina. In Oklahoma, longtime educator Robert Franklin (R), a registered  
Democrat  until  2022,  won  the  open  seat  on  a  promise  to  depoliticize  the  office  after  the  tenure  of  former  
Superintendent  Ryan  Walters  (R).  In  Wyoming,  former  House  Speaker  Steve  Harshman  (R)  defeated  Ana  
Cordova  (D)  75%  to  25%  for  the  seat  left  open  by  Superintendent  Megan  Degenfelder  (R),  who  lost  the  
Republican primary for governor. Democrats will now hold two of the six partisan offices on the ballot, up from  
none.

## [PDF page 16]
Other Statewide Races
STATE AUDITORS  
Fourteen state auditor offices were on the ballot this year, six held by Democrats and eight by Republicans.  
Before the election, Republicans held 23 auditor offices nationally to Democrats’ 14, with one unaffiliated. In  
Ohio, Secretary of State Frank LaRose (R) won the open seat, leading Annette Blackwell (D) 50.8% to 49.2% with  
98% reporting when Blackwell conceded. In Iowa, the race remains uncalled, with Taylor Wettach (D) leading  
Lieutenant Governor Chris Cournoyer (R) 50.2% to 49.8%, a margin of roughly 5,500 votes, for the seat vacated  
by Governor-elect Rob Sand (D). If Wettach’s lead holds, neither seat will change parties.
STATE PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSIONERS  
Nine  states  held  public  service  commissioner  elections  this  year:  Alabama,  Arizona,  Georgia,  Louisiana,  
Montana,  Nebraska,  North  Dakota,  Oklahoma  and  South  Dakota.  Republicans  entered  with  majorities  on  all  
nine commissions. The fight centered on Georgia, where Democrats unseated two Republican commissioners  
in 2025 amid voter frustration over rising power bills and data centers. This year, Democrats won both seats on  
the  ballot,  as  Commissioner  Peter  Hubbard  (D)  defeated  former  Commissioner  Fitz  Johnson  (R)  and  Shelia  
Edwards  (D)  flipped  the  open  District  5  seat,  giving  Democrats  a  3-2  majority  for  the  first  time  in  decades.  
Georgia was the only commission to change party control.
texts.33:
## [PDF page 16]
In Arizona, Democrats ended single-party control of the Corporation Commission. Campaigning on data center  
transparency and utility costs, Clara Pratte (D) and Jonathon Hill (D) defeated Commissioner Kevin Thompson  
(R) and state Representative Ralph Heap (R), leaving Republicans with a 3-2 majority. Pratte, a member of the  
Navajo Nation, becomes the first Indigenous woman elected statewide in Arizona. Louisiana moved the other  
way. Republicans won both open seats, and Caddo Parish Commissioner John Atkins (R) flipped District 5, held  
by Democrats since its creation in 1974, expanding the Republican majority to 4-1.
Republicans held their ground elsewhere. In Alabama, Matt Gentry (R) and Jim Zeigler (R) each won with about  
55%, a closer margin than usual for the state. In Oklahoma, state Representative Brad Boles (R), who sponsored  
the state’s data center law, won the open seat. Republicans also swept the seats on the ballot in North Dakota,  
South  Dakota  and  Montana,  where  the  commission  remains  all-Republican,  as  it  has  been  since  2012.  
Nebraska’s open District 2 remains uncalled, as state Senator Wendy DeBoer (D) seeks to return a Democrat to  
the all-Republican commission against Dennis McCann (R).

## [PDF page 16]
AGRICULTURAL COMMISSIONERS  
Seven states elected agriculture commissioners or their equivalent on November 3. Democrats flipped Texas  
and Georgia, and Republicans held the other five. In Texas, rancher Clayton Tucker (D) defeated Nate Sheets (R)  
51% to 47%, becoming the state’s first Democratic agriculture commissioner in nearly 40 years. Sheets had  
ousted  three-term  Commissioner  Sid  Miller  (R)  in  the  March  primary.  In  Georgia,  Katherine  Juhan-Arnold  (D)  
unseated  one-term  Commissioner  Tyler  Harper  (R)  54%  to  46%.  Republicans  held  the  remaining  offices.  
Commissioner Wilton Simpson (R) won reelection in Florida with 51%, Secretary of Agriculture Mike Naig (R)  
won  a  third  full  term  in  Iowa,  and  Commissioner  Doug  Goehring  (R)  was  reelected  in  North  Dakota.  Cody  
Simpson  (R)  won  South  Carolina’s  open  seat  52%  to  46%,  and  Corey  Hill  (R)  won  Alabama’s  open  seat,  
defeating former Commissioner Ron Sparks (D).

## [PDF page 17]
State Legislatures
Voters in 46 states filled 6,139 legislative seats across 88 chambers on November 3. Democrats  
flipped  at  least  10  chambers  and  lead  in  two  more,  based  on  unofficial  results.  Republicans  
entered the night holding 57 of 99 chambers to Democrats’ 39. If current results hold, Democrats  
would control 51 chambers to Republicans’ 46, the first Democratic chamber edge in more than a  
decade.
ALASKA: Alaska is the only state where both legislative chambers are run by bipartisan coalitions  
of Democrats, independents and moderate Republicans, even though Republicans hold the most  
seats in each. Before the election, the House coalition held the bare minimum of 21 seats needed  
to  govern,  while  the  Senate  coalition  held  a  wider  14-6  edge.  Results  show  the  coalitions  
potentially expanding their control: Democrats and independents lead in 23 of 40 House races  
and have flipped at least two Republican-held seats, while no member of the 14-member Senate  
coalition trails a conservative challenger. Many races are headed to ranked-choice tabulation, so  
final results are not expected until later this month. If the coalitions hold and Democrat Jonathan  
Kreiss-Tomkins wins the uncalled governor’s race, Alaska would have its first governor in years  
working with a Legislature led by allies rather than opponents.
ARIZONA: Republicans held narrow majorities in both chambers before the election, 33-27 in the  
House and 17-13 in the Senate. Democrats flipped the Senate, which they last controlled in 1992,  
and lead in 37 of 60 House races, putting them on track to win the chamber for the first time since  
1966. If the House result holds, Governor Katie Hobbs (D) would begin her second term with the  
state’s first Democratic trifecta in 60 years. The House may not be called for several days while  
ballots are still being counted.
texts.36:
## [PDF page 17]
COLORADO: Democrats already held a trifecta in Colorado and expanded their House majority to  
two-thirds. Paired with Governor-elect Phil Weiser (D), the new supermajority brings Democrats  
closer to the two-thirds needed in both chambers to refer constitutional amendments to voters.
FLORIDA: Republicans kept control of both chambers but lost the supermajorities they had held  
in each, as Democrats flipped at least 16 House seats and a Senate seat (final counts are still  
being  tabulated).  With  Governor-elect  Byron  Donalds  (R)  in  office,  the  change  does  not  affect  
vetoes, but Republicans will now need Democratic votes for anything requiring a two-thirds vote.
GEORGIA: Republicans have controlled both chambers of the General Assembly for more than  
two  decades,  holding  the  House  100-80  after  the  2024  election.  Governor-elect  Keisha  Lance  
Bottoms’  (D)  win  broke  the  Republican  trifecta  in  place  since  2005.  Democrats  have  also  
declared a majority in the House, which they have not held since 2002, though the chamber has  
not been called. Republicans kept control of the Senate but lost their supermajority.
PAGE 15

## [PDF page 18]
State Legislatures
IOWA: Republicans have held a trifecta in Iowa since 2017, along with exactly two-thirds of both  
chambers, the threshold needed to override a veto. Governor-elect Rob Sand’s (D) win ended the  
trifecta, and Democrats broke the Republican supermajority in the House. Because veto overrides  
in  Iowa  require  two-thirds  of  both  chambers,  Sand’s  vetoes  will  hold  even  though  Republicans  
kept their majorities.
KANSAS:  Kansas  had  divided  government  before  the  election,  with  Republicans  holding  
supermajorities of 88-37 in the House and 31-9 in the Senate and routinely overriding Governor  
Laura Kelly (D). Democrats broke the House supermajority, the only chamber on the ballot. If state  
Senator  Cindy  Holscher  (D)  holds  her  narrow  lead  in  the  uncalled  governor’s  race,  her  vetoes  
would be far harder to override than Kelly’s.
MICHIGAN: Control of the Legislature was split before the election, with Republicans holding the  
House 58-52 and Democrats holding the Senate 20-18. Democrats held the Senate and flipped the  
House, and with Governor-elect Jocelyn Benson (D), the party regains the trifecta it lost after the  
2024 election.
MINNESOTA: The House has been tied at 67-67 under a power-sharing agreement, and the DFL  
held the Senate 34-33. The DFL won the House outright and held the Senate, returning the party to  
a trifecta with Governor-elect Amy Klobuchar (DFL).
MISSOURI:  Republicans  kept  control  of  both  chambers,  but  Democrats  ended  their  
supermajorities in each, picking up at least 15 House seats and 2 Senate seats. Governor Mike  
Kehoe (R) still works with Republican majorities, but measures requiring a two-thirds vote, such as  
emergency clauses that let laws take effect immediately, will now need Democratic support.
texts.38:
## [PDF page 18]
NEVADA: Democrats controlled both chambers before the election but were each one seat short  
of the two-thirds needed to override Governor Joe Lombardo’s (R) vetoes. Governor-elect Aaron  
Ford’s (D) win gives Democrats a trifecta for the first time since 2023, and the party also won a  
two-thirds supermajority in the Assembly. Nevada requires a two-thirds vote in each chamber to  
raise taxes, so Democrats will still need Republican support in the Senate to pass any revenue  
increase.
NEW HAMPSHIRE: Before the election, Republicans held the 400-member House by more than 30  
seats and the Senate 16-8. Democrats flipped both chambers, ending the Republican trifecta even  
as Governor Kelly Ayotte (R) won reelection, and now control the full General Court for the first  
time  since  2018.  Democrats  won  a  two-thirds  majority  in  the  House,  while  one  Senate  race  
remains within recount range.
NEW  YORK:  Democrats  expanded  their  Senate  majority  to  a  supermajority,  strengthening  their  
hand alongside Governor Kathy Hochul (D).
NORTH  CAROLINA:  Before  the  election,  Republicans  held  the  Senate  30-20,  exactly  enough  to  
override Governor Josh Stein’s (D) vetoes, and the House 71-47, one seat short. Democrats flipped  
the House for the first time since 2010 and broke the Senate supermajority, so Stein’s vetoes will  
now hold in both chambers after two years of overrides.

## [PDF page 19]
State Legislatures
OHIO: Republicans held a trifecta before the election, with veto-proof majorities of 65-34 in the  
House  and  24-9  in  the  Senate.  Governor-elect  Amy  Acton’s  (D)  win  ended  the  trifecta,  and  
Democrats broke the House supermajority. Because Ohio requires three-fifths of both chambers  
to override a veto, Acton’s vetoes will hold, although Republicans kept their supermajority in the  
Senate.
PENNSYLVANIA: Before the election, Democrats held the House 103-100, and Republicans held  
the Senate 27-23. In one of the night’s most significant results, Democrats held the House and  
flipped the Senate, giving Pennsylvania a trifecta for the first time since 1993.
SOUTH  CAROLINA:  Republicans  kept  control  of  both  chambers,  but  Democrats  broke  the

TEXAS: Republicans held the House 88-62 before the election. Democrats flipped the chamber,  
winning control for the first time since the 2002 election, while Republicans held the Senate 19-12.  
With  Governor-elect  Gina  Hinojosa’s  (D)  win  breaking  the  Republican  trifecta,  Texas  now  has

VERMONT: Republicans made surprising gains in 2024, breaking Democratic supermajorities in

Senate.  Scott  won  a  record  sixth  term,  but  Democrats  will  now  have  the  votes  to  override  his  
vetoes, the most consequential supermajority change of the night.

WISCONSIN:  Republicans  held  the  Assembly  54-45  and  the  Senate  18-15  before  the  election,  
under maps first used in 2024. Democrats flipped both chambers for the first time since 2010, and
